data.name: Last Salvo
data.detailed_description:
The Soviet–Japanese war of 1939

Play through 2 world war two singleplayer campaigns centered around the Battles of Khalkhin Gol between the Empire of Japan and the USSR.
Estimated play time: 20 hours per campaign.
Early access features only the battle for Lake Khasan campaign.

Master different weapons

Destroy enemies superior in number and in firepower by mastering suppressive fire, piercing rounds, explosions, fire barrages, and smokescreens.

Destructible environments

Anything can be destroyed and in the meantime can provide cover from grenade blasts and fire.

Vicious AI

Enemies will try their best to survive by avoiding line of fire, grenades and burning ground. Different behavior types must be expected.

Modding

New units, weapons and campaign can be created, using Lua scripting language.

reviews.review:
Pros:
-Solid controls
-Difficult (if you like that)
-Addictive gameplay (feels a little like hotline miami with the amount of enemies you have to process at once)
-when you die you restart the mission 

Cons:
-The trailer kind of tricked me a little because it seems like you are always in a big battle (you are at the start but when your ai dies which they always do you are alone until you get to a certain part of the map then you sometimes get reinforcements depending on the mission) it might change in late missions I'm not sure yet but right now it feels like you are Japanese Rambo
-Ai.. so the ai is weird, it seems your friendly AI sucks while the enemy AI is a little too clever. It seems to know when you are out of ammo and also preemtively dodge your bullets (also something that ticks me off is that dogs dodge bullets)
-The timings are a little off.. so the devs claim each mission will take you 2 hours+ minimum. it took me 50 minutes on the hardest difficulty to beat the first 2 missions. so yeah.. devs your game testers suck :P
-melee hit boxes are weird. so like with the bayonet you need to be pressed right against someone to hit them and sometimes then it phases through them for no reason
-Enemy machine guns.. so yeah it would be nice if melee could attack upwards a little bit because otherwise without grenades you need to run infront of an mg to shoot at it (that does not end well)
-sometimes it feels like false difficulty like where after a long difficult part in i think mission 2 you come up to 2 pens full of dogs that rush you forcing you to continually run back and the dogs obviously know to dodge your bullets so hitting them is basically looking away from them then snapping your view back at them for maybe a frame getting one pistol shot on them then keep running because the rifle aims and shoots to slowly so you cant one shot the dogs and theres like 12 of them (as you can tell this was the part that was most time consuming of the first two missions)

Wishlist:
-More than just Russia and Japan (hopefully modders will solve this though)
-maybe a kind of killstreak system where you can call in reinforcements after you take down a bunch of enemies
-ability to pick up weapons off the floor (its annoying not being able to do that)
-multiplayer (don't know if its planned but that would be the best thing that could happen to this game)
-maybe like a commander mode where it becomes a stratagy game where you watch and send soldiers in
-instead of a difficulty system you could add a custom class where giving yourself more things make you get less points (still not sure what those points are adding up for. I know it says they unlock loadouts but that is not very clear what it's unlocking if it is)

Conclusion:
-Keeping the game i really enjoy it and i hope there is more content in the future but there are a few things that make me a little frustrated.
-you have to be extra patient because the ai dodges bullets so if you a super aggressive player this aint the game for you
reviews.developer_response:
Hello thank you for your feedback. To be honest with you I had almost no testers. It's difficult to find people attracted to that kind of game and can give relevant feedback. That's why I'm releasing in early access. By the way I'm the only developer (graphics/programming/sounds/testing).

Early missions are meant to be easier, 2h is an average, then it gets harder. I'm still tweaking the difficulty. You're right that missions can be unequal, that's something I need to work on.

You can use molotov cocktails to run away from the dogs as they would not follow you into the fire. Grenades can be used in a suppressive role combined with gun attack (to make enemies flee while you shoot at them).

In this mission dogs are enclosed between crates so if you come early enough before they escape you can grenade them.

Dogs are meant to be a pain in the ass to deal with. I know this is not what you usually see in video games but I won't change it too much unless lots of people complain. Maybe I can bring them only later into the game or something.

Enemies do know when you're reloading and attack you at that time on purpose, yes.

I want to add different factions but I will focus on gameplay on missions for now. But this is the end goal. 

The idea of the current loadout system is that each mission forces you to play a different style. I will probably depart from that in the future, I thought it would be easier to manage for a first release.

Commander mode is totally doable. Maybe the game could turn into some mount and and blade thing, with procedurally generated missions and squads that you can control. I want to deliver a reasonably finished product before I start exploring.

There is a mission where the enemy bullet dodge is disabled. Modders will be able to do it.

The game has been designed from the ground up not to be multiplayer, unfortunately. The engine could be converted to multiplayer but this is not planned for now. I think if single player is solid enough it could give an incentive for it but for now I need to consolidate.
